tests.title: Open the global search palette with the keyboard shortcut (⌘K / Ctrl+K)
tests.refs: SV-9160 (PRD 5.1 Trigger and Surface; 8 Functional Requirements)
tests.custom_preconds: 1. Sign in to ShopView and go to any page, for example the Work Orders list. The persistent search field in the app header shows the shortcut hint (for example 'Search ⌘K').
tests.custom_steps:
1. Without clicking anything, press ⌘K (Ctrl+K on Windows), as shown in the header search field.
2. Watch the screen.
tests.custom_expected:
1. A centered search box (a modal overlay, 640px wide) opens on top of the page, positioned 96px from the top — it is NOT anchored to the header field.

2. The page behind the box is dimmed.

3. The search input is focused so you can type right away, and shows the placeholder 'Search work orders, customers, parts and more' (no 'ask a question' / AI wording — AI is out of scope in v1).

4. The footer keyboard legend is visible: ↓↑ Navigate · ⏎ Select · Esc Close.

This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-9160 and the Global Search - Product Requirements specification version 1.5 (Confluence page 576978945), section 5.1 (trigger and surface), read on 16 September 2026.

Note: earlier this case gave only 'a plain search placeholder'. Spec v1.3 (2026-09-01, §5.1) fixes the exact placeholder and that the modal is centered (not anchored to the header); this case follows the current spec.

Last checked against build v26.36.7-21b4db9 on 9/16/2026.

tests.title: The scope tab strip lists All plus the eight entity tabs in the exact order
tests.refs: SV-9160 (PRD 5.2 tab strip - ten tabs)
tests.custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to ShopView. In the app header, click the search field (or press ⌘K / Ctrl+K) to open the global search, which searches across work orders, customers, parts and more; results appear grouped by type under a tab strip.
2. Sign in as a user whose role can view every entity type - work orders, customers, assets, parts, vendors, part sales, purchase orders and vendor invoices - otherwise a tab is hidden for any type you cannot see.
3. Have at least one matching record of each type for one short query: make sure there exist work orders, customers, assets, parts, vendors, part sales, purchase orders and vendor invoices that all share the same few letters in their name or number (for example all containing 'Fib').
tests.custom_steps:
1. Type the shared few letters (for example 'Fib') so results appear across every type.
2. Read the horizontal tab strip directly under the search box, left to right, scrolling it sideways to reveal all of the tabs.
3. Confirm the order reads: All, Work Orders, Customers, Assets, Parts, Vendors, Part Sales, Purchase Orders, Vendor Invoices, and that there is no Contacts tab.
4. Read the count shown in parentheses on each tab.
5. Confirm the 'All' tab is the one selected by default.
tests.custom_expected:
1. The tabs read, in this exact left-to-right order: All, Work Orders, Customers, Assets, Parts, Vendors, Part Sales, Purchase Orders, Vendor Invoices.

2. There is no Contacts tab.

3. The 'All' tab is selected by default.

4. Each tab carries its total result count over the full result set (for example 'All (12)', 'Work Orders (8)').

5. The strip scrolls sideways, since the nine tabs (All plus eight entity tabs) do not all fit the 640px-wide search box.

6. A tab is shown only for an entity type the user has permission to see.

This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-9160 and the Global Search - Product Requirements specification version 1.5 (Confluence page 576978945), section 5.2 (tab strip), read on 16 September 2026.

tests.title: Selecting a scope tab shows only that entity's results with its count
tests.refs: SV-9160 (PRD 5.2 scope tab scoping)
tests.custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to ShopView. In the app header, click the search field (or press ⌘K / Ctrl+K) to open the global search, which searches across work orders, customers, parts and more; results appear grouped by type under a tab strip.
2. Have a term that returns MORE THAN 20 matches in at least one entity group - for example make sure there are at least 21 work orders whose number or customer name share the same few letters.
tests.custom_steps:
1. Type the term that matches more than 20 records in one group.
2. On the 'All' tab, note that each group shows up to five rows with a 'Show all N' link on its heading.
3. Click that entity's scope tab.
4. Scroll the scoped list inside the modal and confirm it shows up to 20 rows, with no pagination, no further loading, and no 'Show all' link inside the tab.
5. Confirm the tab's count reads 20, not the higher true number.
6. Confirm you stay inside the search modal - selecting the tab did not open a separate results page.
tests.custom_expected:
1. Selecting an entity scope tab scopes the query to that entity type only.

2. The scoped tab shows up to 20 rows, scrolled inside the modal - there is no pagination, no further loading, and no 'Show all' link inside the tab.

3. The scope tab's count never reads higher than 20; a query with more than 20 matches shows the count as 20.

4. You stay inside the search modal - selecting a tab does not open a separate results page.

This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-9160 and the Global Search - Product Requirements specification version 1.5 (Confluence page 576978945), section 5.2 (scope tabs; counts capped at 20), read on 16 September 2026.

Note: spec v1.4 (2026-09-04) drops the earlier full-page 'Show all' hand-off (term placed in the list's search box, filters reset) and caps every count at 20; 'Show all' now switches to an in-modal scope tab. This case follows the current spec.

tests.title: Status and stock badges in search match the rest of the app
tests.refs: SV-9160 (PRD 5.3 result row anatomy - shared badge component and status-to-tone map); SV-9170
tests.custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to ShopView as a user who can see Work Orders and Parts.

2. Know how to open the search: click the search field in the app header, or press Ctrl+K (Cmd+K on a Mac). It searches across work orders, customers, parts and more, and groups the results under a row of tabs.

3. Have a customer whose work orders cover every status. On the branch used for this run that is ZZAUTOTEST Fibridge Commercial: from the top menu choose Work Orders, click Search on the toolbar and type the customer name.

4. Be able to reach the parts list: from the top menu choose Parts, then Inventory. Its toolbar carries a Supply menu with All, Under-supplied, Well-supplied and Over-supplied.

5. Note: an Imported work order cannot be created in the app - those records only arrive by data import. If none exists on the branch, record that status as not checkable rather than guessing.
tests.custom_steps:
Part A - work order status colours

  1. Open Work Orders and search the toolbar for the customer named in the preconditions.
  2. Open the Status menu and tick one status only, starting with Estimate.
  3. Write down the colour shown in the Status column and the work order number of one of the rows.
  4. Repeat steps 2 and 3 for every status in the menu in turn: Approved, In progress, Review, Complete, Invoiced, Paid, Declined, Imported.
  5. Press Ctrl+K, type the same customer name and click the Work orders tab.
  6. Find each work order number you wrote down and compare the colour of its status against what you wrote down for it.
  7. Look at the whole list of results together and check whether any two different statuses are showing the same colour as each other.

Part B - part stock colours

  1. Open Parts, then Inventory.
  2. Open the Supply menu and choose Under-supplied.
  3. Write down the colour shown under Total Quantity and the part number of one of the rows.
  4. Repeat for Well-supplied and then for Over-supplied.
  5. Press Ctrl+K, type the first part number, wait for the results to settle, and click the Parts tab.
  6. Match the row by its description, not only by the number - two different parts can share a part number - and compare its quantity colour against what you wrote down.
  7. Repeat for the other two part numbers.
tests.custom_expected:
A work order's status and a part's stock level are shown in the same colour in the search as they are in the rest of the app. The search does not keep a set of colours of its own; it takes each one from the shared set the rest of the product uses, so that a colour changed once changes everywhere.

Because of that:

  • every status keeps its own colour in the search, exactly as it appears on the Work Orders list;
  • two statuses a person needs to tell apart are never shown in the same colour;
  • a part's quantity keeps the colour the Parts list gives it - under-supplied, well-supplied and over-supplied each stay distinct.

No particular colour value is fixed by the requirement. What is required is that the search and the rest of the app agree, whatever the shared set says today.

Source:

  • Epic SV-9160.
  • Global Search - Product Requirements, Confluence page 576978945, version 17 (the document's own change log calls it v1.5, last updated 8 September 2026), section 5.3 Result row anatomy, read on 17 September 2026. It reads: "Status badges come from the design system. Search uses the shared Badge component and the system's status-to-tone map; it does not define a palette of its own. Any change to a status colour is made in the design system and propagates here, so no colour values are pinned in this document." And: "Stock badges on parts use the same component."

Corrected on 17 September 2026 with the QA lead's go-ahead. The earlier version of this case listed fixed colours per status - Approved green, Estimate blue, Review yellow, In Progress blue, Completed gray, Declined red, Invoiced purple - which came from an older copy of the document. The page read live no longer pins any colour, so that list has been replaced by the rule it actually states.

tests.title: Permission bundles hide whole groups, their counts and tabs; prices masked without financial access
tests.custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to ShopView. In the app header, click the search field (or press ⌘K / Ctrl+K) to open the global search, which searches across work orders, customers, parts and more; results appear grouped by type under a tab strip.

2. Be able to sign in as several roles, each missing exactly one view bundle in turn: no 'Work Orders: View'; no 'Part Sales: View'; no 'Customers: View'; no 'Catalog & Inventory: View'; no 'Vendor & Order Management: View'. Also a role without 'See Financial Data', and a TimeClock-only user.

3. Records exist across all eight entity types matching one term, including priced records (a part with purchase/sell price, a part sale, a work order total, a PO total and a vendor-invoice total).
tests.custom_steps:
1. Sign in as the role missing 'Work Orders: View', search the term, and confirm no Work Orders group, count or scope tab appears.

2. Repeat for each bundle in turn: missing 'Part Sales: View' hides Part Sales; missing 'Customers: View' hides Customers AND Assets; missing 'Catalog & Inventory: View' hides Parts; missing 'Vendor & Order Management: View' hides Vendors, Purchase Orders AND Vendor Invoices.

3. Each time, confirm the hidden group leaks neither its rows nor its count, and no scope tab appears for it.

4. Sign in without 'See Financial Data', search, and confirm every price field is masked (part purchase/sell price, part-sale total, work-order total, PO total, vendor-invoice total).

5. Sign in as a TimeClock-only user, search anything, and confirm no results appear that the user is not permitted to see.
tests.custom_expected:
1. Permission filtering follows the eight-entity bundle mapping: Work Orders → Work Orders: View; Part Sales → Part Sales: View; Customers and Assets → Customers: View; Parts → Catalog & Inventory: View; Vendors, Purchase Orders and Vendor Invoices → Vendor & Order Management: View. (A contact match rides its parent company's Customers/Vendor permission.)

2. A hidden entity group leaks neither its rows nor its count, and no scope tab appears for it.

3. Without 'See Financial Data', the money fields shown inside result rows are masked. Per section 4 the result rows that display a money field are the Part Sale (“total price”), the Purchase Order (“total”) and the Vendor Invoice (“total”); a Part row and a Work Order row are not listed with a price, so there is no money field to mask on them.

4. A TimeClock-only user sees no results they are not permitted to see.

Source:

  • Epic SV-9160 and the Global Search - Product Requirements specification version 1.5 (Confluence page 576978945), section 9: “All result fields must respect existing tenant-isolation and role-based-access checks.”
  • The engineering resolution recorded on that page (2026-08-12): “results, group counts and scope tabs are all filtered by the user's permissions” and “'See Financial Data' gates prices inside result rows”.
  • Section 4 displayed fields, verbatim: Part Sales “total price + created date”; Purchase Orders “total + created date”; Vendor Invoices “total + invoice date”; Parts “description (primary), part number (secondary), total quantity with a stock-status badge” (no price); Work Orders “WO number + customer name (primary), status badge, unit number + year/make/model” (no total).

Corrected on 21 September 2026 to quote section 4: the masked money fields are only the part-sale total, the purchase-order total and the vendor-invoice total (part price and work-order total removed - section 4 does not display them). Read on 21 September 2026.

1. Sign in to ShopView. In the app header, click the search field (or press ⌘K / Ctrl+K) to open the global search, which searches across work orders, customers, parts and more; results appear grouped by type under a tab strip.

2. A part exists (visible to a permitted user) whose name a typo query would match.

3. You are signed in as a user whose role does NOT include Catalog & Inventory (parts) access.
tests.custom_steps:
1. Type a misspelled version of that part’s name (a typo the fuzzy match would normally catch).

2. Read the grouped results in the search palette, looking at the Parts group.
tests.custom_expected:
The part you are not allowed to see is NOT returned by the typo match. Access is applied to fuzzy matches too, not only to exact matches.

Records you ARE allowed to see still fuzzy-match normally.

This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-9160 and the Global Search - Product Requirements specification version 1.5 (Confluence page 576978945), section 9 and section 7 (role-based access applies to fuzzy matches as well as exact matches), read on 18 September 2026.

Note: fuzzy matching widens what is found, so it needs its own access check.

Last checked against build v26.36.8-d146c39 on 18 September 2026.

tests.title: Flipping only Parts access shows then hides the same part in search
tests.custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to ShopView. In the app header, click the search field (or press ⌘K / Ctrl+K) to open the global search, which searches across work orders, customers, parts and more; results appear grouped by type under a tab strip.

2. Seed ONE specific part tagged ZZAUTOTEST that matches a unique query.

3. Have TWO roles that are identical in every way EXCEPT the 'Catalog & Inventory: View' access: one WITH it, one WITHOUT it (or one user whose 'Catalog & Inventory: View' access you can turn off between the two runs). Use the SAME query for both runs so only the permission differs.

Use the keyword ZZTOGPART (the seeded part 'ZZTOGPART Brake Kit').
tests.custom_steps:
1. As the role WITH 'Catalog & Inventory: View' access, type the query and confirm the seeded record appears.

2. Switch to the identical role WITHOUT 'Catalog & Inventory: View' access (or turn that access off for the same user), type the SAME query, and look for the SAME record.

3. Allow a moment for the index if the record was just seeded before deciding it is absent.
tests.custom_expected:
With access, the seeded part appears in the 'Parts' group and its scope tab.

Without access, the SAME part is gone: no 'Parts' group, no row, no count for it.

Nothing else changed between the two runs, so the record can only have disappeared because the permission was removed.

This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-9160 and the Global Search - Product Requirements specification version 1.5 (Confluence page 576978945), section 9 (results, group counts and scope tabs are all filtered by the user's permissions), read on 18 September 2026.

Same-record toggle: rules out 'the part did not exist / did not match / had not indexed' as the reason it was hidden.

Last checked against build v26.36.8-d146c39 on 18 September 2026.

tests.title: Removing See Financial Data hides the total on a Vendor invoice row but keeps the row
tests.custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to ShopView. In the app header, click the search field (or press ⌘K / Ctrl+K) to open the global search, which searches across work orders, customers, parts and more; results appear grouped by type under a tab strip.

  2. Have TWO roles that are identical except for the "See Financial Data" permission - one with it, one without. The same person can be moved between them.

  3. Pick a word that returns at least one Vendor invoice. "truck repair" works on the test branch.

A Vendor invoice row is the right row for this check: it is one of the rows that prints a total. A part row never prints a price at all, so the price cannot be watched appearing and disappearing there.
tests.custom_steps:
1. Signed in as the role WITH "See Financial Data", type the word and open the "Vendor invoices" tab.

  2. Read the first row and note the total shown on it, and the invoice number next to it.

  3. Move the same person to the role WITHOUT "See Financial Data" and sign in again.

  4. Type the SAME word, open the "Vendor invoices" tab and find the SAME invoice number.
tests.custom_expected:
With the See Financial Data permission, the vendor-invoice row shows its invoice number and vendor, its status, and its total.

Without the See Financial Data permission, the same vendor-invoice row still appears with its invoice number, vendor and status, but its total is not shown. The permission gates the money figures shown inside result rows; it does not remove the record.

Source:

  • Epic SV-9160 and the Global Search - Product Requirements specification version 1.5 (Confluence page 576978945), section 4, which lists a Vendor Invoice result's displayed fields verbatim: “invoice number + vendor (primary), status badge (Paid / Unpaid), total + invoice date”.
  • The same specification, section 9: “All result fields must respect existing tenant-isolation and role-based-access checks.”
  • The engineering resolution recorded on that page (2026-08-12): “'See Financial Data' gates prices inside result rows.”

The check is placed on a vendor-invoice row because section 4 lists a total among its displayed fields; section 4 lists no price among a Part row's displayed fields, so a part row has no money field to gate. Read on 21 September 2026.

tests.title: Records a person cannot see are not counted in any heading, tab or total
tests.custom_preconds:
1. Sign in to ShopView. In the app header, click the search field (or press ⌘K / Ctrl+K) to open the global search, which searches across work orders, customers, parts and more; results appear grouped by type under a tab strip.

  2. Have TWO roles that are identical except that one is missing a whole access area - for example "Part Sales: View". The same person can be moved between them.

  3. Pick a word that returns results of several kinds at once. "truck repair" works on the test branch.

Permissions on this product grant or deny a whole KIND of record, never one individual record. This check is therefore written around a kind of record being taken away, which is the only way a record can be made unreachable here.
tests.custom_steps:
1. Signed in as the role WITH the access area, type the word.

  2. On the "All" tab, write down the number shown on the "All" tab itself, and the number shown on each group heading and on each tab in the strip.

  3. Move the same person to the role WITHOUT that access area and sign in again.

  4. Type the SAME word and read the same numbers again.
tests.custom_expected:
For a kind of record the person is allowed to see: that kind has its own group heading and its own scope tab, each showing its result count, and its results are included on the All tab.

For a kind of record the person is not allowed to see: no group, no count and no scope tab appears for that kind, and none of its records are counted anywhere. Results, group counts and scope tabs are all filtered by the person's permissions.

Every count shown is capped, so no count in the search reads higher than twenty.

Source:

  • Epic SV-9160 and the Global Search - Product Requirements specification version 1.5 (Confluence page 576978945), section 9: “All result fields must respect existing tenant-isolation and role-based-access checks - a technician without Parts access does not see Parts results.”
  • The engineering resolution recorded on that page (2026-08-12): “results, group counts and scope tabs are all filtered by the user's permissions.”
  • The same specification, section 5.2: “No count in the modal reads higher than 20.”

Access is granted by kind of record, so this is verified by turning a whole kind on and off. Read on 21 September 2026.

tests.title: Global search works on mobile/tablet viewports per the mobile design
tests.custom_preconds:
1. On a phone (or a narrow, phone-sized browser window below the small breakpoint), sign in to ShopView and tap the search field in the app header to open the full-screen global search, which searches across work orders, customers, parts and more; results appear grouped by type and you tap a row to open its record.
2. Have a query that matches records across several types, with MORE THAN five matches in at least one group, so you can confirm results are not capped.
tests.custom_steps:
1. Type the term so grouped results appear.
2. Confirm the search fills the whole screen (not a centered modal) and the page does not scroll sideways.
3. Look at the scope selection: confirm it is a horizontal chip row that appears only once there is a query, listing only the types that actually matched (each with its count), with no Contacts chip.
4. Scroll a group with more than five matches and confirm ALL its matches are shown - there is no per-group cap and no 'Show all' link.
5. Tap a row and confirm it opens the record; confirm rows show no hover quick actions on mobile.
tests.custom_expected:
1. The global search is a full-screen screen on mobile (not a centered modal), matching the Mobile Global Search design, with no horizontal scroll.

2. Scope selection is a horizontal chip row that appears only once there is a query, and lists only the entity types that actually matched (each with its count) — not the full nine-tab strip. There is no Contacts chip.

3. Rows carry no hover quick actions on mobile; a tap opens the record, and every action remains reachable from the record.

4. Results are not capped per group and there is no 'Show all' overflow — the user scrolls the full grouped list.

This is the expected behaviour as per epic SV-9160 and the Global Search - Product Requirements specification version 1.5 (Confluence page 576978945), section 5.6 (mobile), read on 16 September 2026.

Note: earlier this case said quick actions are reachable on touch and referenced 'up to ten tabs'. Spec v1.3 (2026-09-01, §5.6) removed Contacts (so it is a matched-types chip row, not ten tabs) and states mobile rows carry no quick actions (tap opens the record); this case follows the current spec.

Last checked against build v26.36.7-21b4db9 on 9/16/2026.

tests.title: Selecting each result type opens the right record
tests.refs: SV-9160 (INV-46; V1 baseline 55767168; Part opened the CATALOGUE part in V1)
tests.custom_preconds: Logged in as Admin (Work Orders: View, Customers: View) A customer with no pinned note, one of its vehicles, and an open work order on that vehicle carrying one labor line — all seeded over the API The work order is present in the search index
tests.custom_steps:
1. Open global search.
2. For each type in turn, type a term that matches a record of that type and click the row.
3. Write down which page opened each time.
4. Do this for the STOCKED part 'ZZT-88-4412'.
5. Do this for the CATALOGUE-ONLY part 'ZZT-77-3300' - search 'Vernway' if the part number returns nothing.
6. For the Asset, check the page you land on belongs to the right owning customer.
tests.custom_expected:
1. Work Order opens the work order page. Part Sale opens the part sale page. Customer opens that customer's work-orders page. Asset opens that asset's work-orders page, for the correct owning customer. Vendor opens the vendor page.
2. A Part opens a part record you can actually use.
3. THE CATALOGUE-ONLY PART IS THE POINT OF THIS CASE. In V1 a Part result opened the CATALOGUE part page, so every part in the catalogue could be reached from search whether or not the shop had ever stocked it. If the catalogue-only part cannot be found at all, or is found but the row leads nowhere, that is a V1 capability that has gone.
IF THAT HAPPENS: mark the test FAILED and write down exactly what you searched and what the row did. It worked in the previous version, so it has to work here. Do not pass the case on the grounds that opening the inventory part is what the newer version intends; this suite asks only whether the previous version's capability survived.
Correction, 14 September 2026: an earlier version of this case was changed to require the INVENTORY part, following specification v1.3. That was wrong for a regression case - V1 is the specification this suite tests against, and V1 opened the catalogue part. The case has been put back and the difference raised as a finding instead.

tests.title: Finding an asset by its make on its own
tests.refs: SV-9160 (INV-04; V1 baseline 55767168; PRD 1.5 s4 Assets)
tests.custom_preconds:
1. Sign in and open global search: click the Search box in the app header, or press Ctrl+K. It opens a centred modal — a search box, a scope-tab strip (All, Work orders, Customers, Assets, Parts, Vendors, Part sales, Purchase orders, Vendor invoices) each with its own count, and results grouped by type with a count on each heading; press Esc to close. Seed check: if a search for ZZAUTOTEST returns nothing the build was redeployed, so ask for a reseed and do not hand-create records.
1. The asset '2019 Freightliner Cascadia', unit number 'ZZT-4471', owned by 'ZZAUTOTEST Bridgeport Hauling', exists.
2. Freightliner is the MAKE. Cascadia is the model. This case tests the make.
3. Customers access: View (assets are shown under Customers access).
tests.custom_steps:
1. Open global search.
2. Type the make on its own: Freightliner
3. Read the Assets group. Look at the make of every vehicle listed.
Type the make and nothing else. Do not add the year or the model - typing the year together with the make is a different test with a different result, and it has its own case.
The list shows a limited number of vehicles per group, and a busy shop has far more vehicles of one make or one year than the list can show. So your seeded vehicle may or may not be among them, and its absence is not a failure - what matters is whether the search used the field at all.
tests.custom_expected:
Every vehicle listed in the Assets group is a Freightliner, and the group is not empty. That is what proves the search looked at the vehicle's make.
In V1 the make was part of what a vehicle could be found by, in its own right - alongside the year, the model, the unit number, the VIN number and the licence plate.

WHAT COUNTS AS A FAILURE, and what does not.
A failure: the Assets group is empty, or vehicles of a DIFFERENT make appear in it.
Not a failure: your own seeded vehicle '2019 Freightliner Cascadia' is not in the list. There are more Freightliners in this data than the list can show, so it may sit below the last row. V1 showed even fewer per group than V2 does, so this was never a case of 'my vehicle must appear' - it is a case of 'the make is searched'. If you want to see that exact vehicle, search its model instead - that is C55664.
Also not a failure: a vehicle whose displayed make looks unrelated but whose VIN number or unit number contains the letters you typed. Open the record and check before calling it wrong - those fields are searched too.

Failed on staging (app.staging.shopview.com), workplace Staging Heavy Duty - 9919, build v26.39.1-02c6b6c, 28 September 2026.

Nothing is recorded when somebody picks a search result.

A search was run, a result was clicked, and every request the page made was watched. The only thing that looks like a record is a Google Analytics message - and it carries the event name "page_view" and does not mention search anywhere. The same message fires when you simply walk to the Parts page without searching at all, so it is an ordinary page view, not a record of the search selection. Nothing is sent to ShopView's own system about the choice that was made.

So there is no way to learn what people search for, what they pick, or whether the search is helping them.

Worth knowing: the written requirements for this version say under Non-Goals that there will be no logging of what people see or click in this release, and the story that would have built it was closed OBSOLETE. So this is almost certainly intended, and this check - which was written against the OLD search - is the thing that is now out of date rather than the product. Retiring it or rewording it is your call; I cannot change what a check expects on my own.

WHAT THE REQUIREMENT ASKS, word for word from the requirements page read live on 23 September, section 7, Highlighting: "When a match is fuzzy rather than exact, the matched token in the row is still highlighted, and a subtle close-match treatment indicates the soft match."

HOW FAR THIS WAS CHECKED. Not a sample. Every field the requirements say each of the eight tabs searches on was exercised, driven off that list rather than off chosen queries: a real value was taken from the branch, misspelled, and the field counted as covered only where the product itself reported a near-spelling match against it. Thirty combinations were reached.

TWENTY-EIGHT ARE CORRECT - the matched text is shown and carries the close-match mark:
  - Jobs: customer name, asset make, asset model, lead technician, line text, part names on the line.
  - Customers: name, address line 1, address line 2, town.
  - Assets: make, model, owning customer.
  - Parts: description, tags, category, manufacturer, supplier name.
  - Suppliers: name, address line 1, address line 2, town.
  - Part sales: customer name, asset.
  - Purchase orders: supplier name, part names on the order, who ordered it.
  - Supplier invoices: supplier name.

TWO ARE WRONG, and both are contact names. Neither half of the requirement is met on them - the contact's name is not shown at all, so there is nothing to pick out, and there is no close-match mark:
  - Customers found through a contact's name: 18 near-spelling rows, none marked, none showing the name. Reported as SV-10346 - https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-10346
  - Suppliers found through a contact's name: 11 near-spelling rows, none marked, none showing the name. Reported as SV-10385 - https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-10385 - raised 23 September on the QA lead's instruction, after the seven unproved fields below were proved.

SEVEN FIELDS WERE PROVED NOT TO MATCH ON NEAR SPELLINGS AT ALL, so they are out of scope rather than untested. Each was proved with a control: the exact value was searched first and did return the record naming that field, which shows the field is indexed and the reading works; the misspelling then returned nothing on it. They are customer telephone, customer state or province, supplier telephone, supplier email, part bin location, asset year, and asset unit number.

  - Marlene: company-name near-spellings 5 of 5 marked; contact-name near-spellings 0 of 4 marked.
  - Darlene: 1 of 1 marked; 0 of 3 marked.
  - Petersn, the requirement's own worked example: 2 of 2 marked; 0 of 14 marked.

Cannot be isolated on this test site, and the honest answer is that I cannot tell whether the rule works. Two jobs were built for the purpose - same customer, same vehicle, same shop, created seconds apart - which makes them equal on everything the ranking scores, so only this rule should decide their order. Every way of nudging one of them either does not reach the search, or is ignored, or moves something stronger. Changing the engine hours saved but search does not look at that field. Assigning a technician reported success and saved nothing at all. Adding a job line DID move that job to the top - but the same change flipped it from Estimate to Approved, and being open is a stronger ranking signal than this rule, so the climb proves nothing. Putting both jobs on the same status to remove that advantage left no way to nudge either of them: the line could not be added a second time.

Not observed this run: Whether the most-recently-changed rule is applied at all. It was nearly reported as broken, and separately nearly reported as working - both would have been wrong.

What needs to be done: one of two things. Either the developers say what makes a job re-enter the search after an edit, so a change can be made that search notices without also changing the job's status - or the same test is done on a record type that shows a last-changed date, since neither customers nor jobs show one anywhere readable. Until then this stays open rather than being called a fault. Nothing else is held up by it.

No report has been written for this yet - it is with the QA lead, who approves each one before it is raised. The evidence is below.

the ruling sits with the Product Owner on SV-10025 - https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-10025. Technical detail: RE-CHECKED ON 18 SEPTEMBER 2026, build v26.36.7-29ca209, after the developer added the line on each row that says how it matched, and asked whether this is still relevant. WHAT CHANGED: each near-spelling row now carries a visible marker reading 'close match', so a person can see why it is there. WHAT DID NOT CHANGE: the list itself. The requirement accepts a near-spelling when it is at least 70 per cent similar, and on a seven-letter word that permits two letters to differ - which is exactly what these five words are. This check exists because the older version could not return them at all, so it is a difference between the two versions for the Product Owner to rule on, not a coding mistake. the newest part sales come first, the ones you created yourself are lifted above the same-day work of another person, and a paid one is lifted slightly above an unpaid one of the same age - all three of the things this check asks for.

Technical detail: THIS WAS BLOCKED THIS MORNING because there were only two part sales that matched any one search word, and they could not show any of the three effects. The records needed were built this evening on the QA lead's standing authority over test data, and every one of them was read back before anything was concluded. WHAT WAS SET UP - six part sales were made findable by the same word: P9160-261 created today by the signed-in person P9160-262 created today, 26 seconds later, by a different person P9160-260 created yesterday by the signed-in person P9160-246 created 28 August, marked Paid P9160-243 created 27 August, not paid P2-13 created 13 March, marked Paid WHAT THE SEARCH RETURNED, in this order: 1. P9160-261 today, mine 2. P9160-260 yesterday, mine 3. P9160-262 today, somebody else's 4. P9160-246 28 August, Paid 5. P2-13 13 March, Paid 6. P9160-243 27 August, not paid WHY THAT IS RIGHT, one requirement at a time: Recency comes first - the three made in the last two days sit above everything older. Your own work is lifted - the one created 26 seconds AFTER mine sits below both of mine, and the only difference between those two records is who made them; they share the same customer, the same day and the same state. Paid gets a small lift - the paid 28 August sale scores 0.89 against 0.84 for the unpaid 27 August one, a difference of 0.05 between two records made a day apart. The requirement asks for exactly 0.05. The same lift is why a paid sale from March still sits above an unpaid one from August: by then the recency boost has faded to nothing on both, which is what the requirement describes. The order was read from the screen as well as from the product's own numbers, and the two agree.

Checked on the test branch. It will be re-checked on Staging before release.

The spoken announcement works and changes as the results change, and the parts of the search a keyboard reaches all show where you are. The one thing that looked like a fault this morning - the Tab key not stepping onto the result lines - turns out to be the product following the recognised way this kind of search is built, not a fault. The results are stepped through with the up and down arrows, which is correct, and our own check is the thing that needs its wording fixed.

Technical detail: MEASURED 17 SEPTEMBER 2026, build v26.36.7-29ca209. WHAT THE CHECK ASKS FOR, AND WHAT WAS SEEN: 1. A spoken announcement of the number of results, changing when the number changes. YES - the page announces '57 results found across 8 categories', and the wording changes with the query ('6 results...', '1 result...'). It is set to announce politely, which is the correct setting. 2. A visible mark showing where the keyboard is. The row of type tabs shows a clear blue outline, two pixels thick, when the keyboard reaches it. The highlighted result line is tinted and the page tells a screen reader which line it is; pressing the down arrow moves both the tint and the announcement to the next line. The typing box shows the usual blinking cursor rather than an outline. WHY THE TAB KEY IS NOT A FAULT: the search is built as a type-ahead box with a list attached - the box is marked as one, the list is marked as a list, and each line is marked as a choice within it. In that arrangement the typing cursor deliberately stays in the box so a person can keep typing, and the up and down arrows move the highlight while the page tells the screen reader which line is highlighted. Tab is not meant to walk the lines. This build does all of that correctly. WHAT OUR CHECK GETS WRONG: its third step says to press Tab repeatedly to move through the box, the tabs, the result lines and the Show all links in turn. That describes an arrangement this kind of search does not use. The step should say to use the up and down arrows for the result lines. The Show all links do not exist on this build at all, which is a separate matter already with the developers. What needs to be done: the QA lead to allow the third step and the wording under it to be corrected so the next person is not sent looking for behaviour the product should not have.

Checked on the test branch. It will be re-checked on Staging before release.

results.comment:
Tested on QA branch sv9160, build v26.36.4-7869ff2, on 15 September 2026.

A new job was created and then searched for by its number, over and over, without reloading or signing out. It did not come back until about 85 seconds had passed. The requirement allows 30. The method is not in doubt, and two separate controls prove it: a new CUSTOMER, created and timed exactly the same way in the same session, came back after 17 seconds; and a new PART SALE for 'ZZAUTOTEST Bridgeport Hauling', created and timed the same way, came back after 9 seconds. So the clock and the search can both see a brand new record well inside the allowed window - jobs are the one kind that cannot.

Not observed this run: One of the three flows in this case was not run: receiving a part through Receive Order was not exercised. The new-job flow and the new-part-sale flow were both timed.

Logged as SV-10056 - "a newly created job is not findable for about 85 seconds": https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-10056

A newly created job needs to be findable within 30 seconds, as the requirement says and as a new part sale and a new customer both already manage. Useful detail for whoever looks: part sales and customers appear within seconds and jobs do not, so jobs are not being refreshed the same way as the rest. The receive-a-part flow still needs running once.

Technical detail: new work order: findable at ~85s, first hit poll 85s, requirement 30s (spec v1.5 section 9). Controls in the same session: new customer 17s, new part sale P9160-254 9s. No reload, no re-auth between polls.

Tested on the QA branch. Everything here will be re-tested on Staging once the change reaches it.

Typing a word selects the first result, and pressing Enter opens it - that part is right. What goes wrong is the mouse: letting the pointer pass over a row on its way somewhere else makes that row the selected one, without clicking it. Moving the mouse right off the list leaves it selected. Closing the search and opening it again leaves it selected. Press Enter and that record opens instead of the top one, with nothing on screen saying the target moved. Checked with the pointer deliberately parked away from the list, and the parking confirmed rather than assumed. The QA lead approved raising this on 15 September 2026, having checked the previous version on production, where typing a word and pressing Enter takes you to the first record.

Logged as SV-10061 - "Enter opens the wrong record: the highlight starts on the 8th row of a long list, and once you click a row that position sticks across later searches": https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-10061

Pressing Enter should open the top result, and whichever row is going to open should be shown as selected so a person can see where Enter will take them. This needs fixing, and is logged.

Technical detail: query 'Truck', 41 rows, pointer parked at 5,5 and verified with document.elementFromPoint. After typing: focused row 1. Pointer moved over row 9 (no click): focused row 9. Pointer moved off the list: focused row 9. Escape then reopen on the same page: query 'Truck' restored and focused row 9 BEFORE typing. Retyped: focused row 9, Enter opened /customers/a6f3a7bb-d3ea-448c-a16b-d3bae64298a8/work-orders. Spec v1.5 section 9 requires the keyboard-focused row to be visually distinguishable from the mouse-hovered row; here hovering IS what sets keyboard focus. Evidence ENTER-HOVER-REOPEN.json, ENTER-HOVER.json; three annotated screenshots in enter-evidence/. TWO EARLIER DESCRIPTIONS OF THIS CASE WERE WITHDRAWN: both were artefacts of our own harness leaving the mouse pointer where it had clicked, which kept a row hovered across reopenings and looked like a stable product fault (L0117).

Tested on the QA branch. Everything here will be re-tested on Staging once the change reaches it.

Typing a word selects the first result, and pressing Enter opens it - that part is right. What goes wrong is the mouse: letting the pointer pass over a row on its way somewhere else makes that row the selected one, without clicking it. Moving the mouse right off the list leaves it selected. Closing the search and opening it again leaves it selected. Press Enter and that record opens instead of the top one, with nothing on screen saying the target moved. Checked with the pointer deliberately parked away from the list, and the parking confirmed rather than assumed. The QA lead approved raising this on 15 September 2026, having checked the previous version on production, where typing a word and pressing Enter takes you to the first record.

Logged as SV-10061 - "Enter opens the wrong record: the highlight starts on the 8th row of a long list, and once you click a row that position sticks across later searches": https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-10061

Pressing Enter should open the top result, and whichever row is going to open should be shown as selected so a person can see where Enter will take them. This needs fixing, and is logged.

Technical detail: query 'Truck', 41 rows, pointer parked at 5,5 and verified with document.elementFromPoint. After typing: focused row 1. Pointer moved over row 9 (no click): focused row 9. Pointer moved off the list: focused row 9. Escape then reopen on the same page: query 'Truck' restored and focused row 9 BEFORE typing. Retyped: focused row 9, Enter opened /customers/a6f3a7bb-d3ea-448c-a16b-d3bae64298a8/work-orders. Spec v1.5 section 9 requires the keyboard-focused row to be visually distinguishable from the mouse-hovered row; here hovering IS what sets keyboard focus. Evidence ENTER-HOVER-REOPEN.json, ENTER-HOVER.json; three annotated screenshots in enter-evidence/. TWO EARLIER DESCRIPTIONS OF THIS CASE WERE WITHDRAWN: both were artefacts of our own harness leaving the mouse pointer where it had clicked, which kept a row hovered across reopenings and looked like a stable product fault (L0117).

Tested on the QA branch. Everything here will be re-tested on Staging once the change reaches it.

A new job was created and then searched for by its number, over and over, without reloading or signing out. It did not come back until about 85 seconds had passed. The requirement allows 30. The method is not in doubt, and two separate controls prove it: a new CUSTOMER, created and timed exactly the same way in the same session, came back after 17 seconds; and a new PART SALE for 'ZZAUTOTEST Bridgeport Hauling', created and timed the same way, came back after 9 seconds. So the clock and the search can both see a brand new record well inside the allowed window - jobs are the one kind that cannot.

Not observed this run: One of the three flows in this case was not run: receiving a part through Receive Order was not exercised. The new-job flow and the new-part-sale flow were both timed.

Logged as SV-10056 - "a newly created job is not findable for about 85 seconds": https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-10056

A newly created job needs to be findable within 30 seconds, as the requirement says and as a new part sale and a new customer both already manage. Useful detail for whoever looks: part sales and customers appear within seconds and jobs do not, so jobs are not being refreshed the same way as the rest. The receive-a-part flow still needs running once.

Technical detail: new work order: findable at ~85s, first hit poll 85s, requirement 30s (spec v1.5 section 9). Controls in the same session: new customer 17s, new part sale P9160-254 9s. No reload, no re-auth between polls.

Tested on the QA branch. Everything here will be re-tested on Staging once the change reaches it.

Typed a word and pressed Enter without touching the arrow keys. The wrong record opened. Two separate things are wrong. On a long list of results, the row the panel highlights on its own is the eighth, not the first - so Enter opens the eighth record. And once you click a row yourself, that POSITION is remembered: searching again keeps the same row number highlighted, including when you search for a completely different word, where that row holds a record with no connection to what you typed. A short search behaves correctly, which is why this looks fine at first glance - lists of a few results start on the first row. Nothing on screen says which row Enter will open. The QA lead approved raising this on 15 September 2026, after checking the previous version on production himself and confirming that typing a word and pressing Enter there takes you to the first record in the list.

Logged as SV-10061 - "Enter opens the wrong record: the highlight starts on the 8th row of a long list, and once you click a row that position sticks across later searches": https://shopview.atlassian.net/browse/SV-10061

Pressing Enter should open the top result, and whichever row is going to open should be shown as selected so a person can see where Enter will take them. This needs fixing, and is logged.

Technical detail: Highlight index with nothing pressed, by list length: 2, 3, 6 and 8 rows -> index 0; 13, 22 and 41 rows -> index 7. After clicking index 4 on 'Truck' (41 rows): same word again -> index 4 highlighted, Enter opened it; different word 'Repair' -> index 4 highlighted, Enter opened /workorders/27eeb282-7196-4b53-a6f1-4f5016022094/lines, unrelated to the click. In an earlier run where the list had shifted, the same index held a different job - so it is the position that persists, not the record. Evidence ENTER-ANNOTATED.json, ENTER-STICKY.json, ENTER-MANY.json; four annotated screenshots in enter-evidence/. CORRECTION: an earlier reading of this case called it a general failure on the strength of two runs of the same query - that was one observation and one replay, since the app remembers the query (L0115).

Tested on the QA branch. Everything here will be re-tested on Staging once the change reaches it.
